A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FMA research work. Their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison. v1 ends after its references without appendices; v3 includes readable Appendices A–D.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original few-shot classification experiments on eleven datasets, cross-dataset transfer results, and backbone, inference and noise ablations.

after.justification: Section 5 retains original classification experiments and expands transfer evaluation. Appendices C and D supply additional statistics and per-dataset experimental results.

M1.justification: Both versions use fixed image–class-text coupling, time-dependent Gaussian augmentation, velocity regression and an early-stopping Euler solver. Renamed text embeddings, newly disclosed architecture details and relocated Algorithms 1–2 do not establish changes to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: The same eleven datasets and few-shot classification task remain. ImageNet-to-other-dataset transfer already appears in v1; extending it to additional feature extractors introduces no new dataset or transfer scenario.

E2.justification: The main eight-method comparison retains all participants. The transfer comparison expands from CoOp with a CLIP reference in v1 Table 2 to include CoCoOp, CLIP-Adapter and CLIP-LoRA in v3 Table 1, also adding FMA applied to CLIP.

E3.justification: Cars replaces UCF in the difficult group, while UCF moves to the easy group, changing the composition of aggregate metrics. The principal shot counts, default ViT-B/16 backbone, inference step size and validation-based stopping-step selection remain unchanged. Newly stated architecture and training-duration details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The existing transfer-robustness question is tested with five feature extractors instead of FMA on CoOp alone, with per-target breakdowns in Appendix D. This broadens evidence about preserving generalization across adaptation methods. The backbone, inference-step and noise-augmentation ablation designs remain essentially unchanged.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix C first reports standard deviations for FMA results across the model-agnostic comparison and p-values against the baselines in Tables 4–5. v1 provides neither. Run counts, seeds and the statistical test remain unspecified, so this establishes additional uncertainty reporting without establishing increased repetitions.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive transfer-result entries and revises CLIP+FMA results in Table 3, including Aircraft 46.4 to 38.1 and EuroSAT 87.9 to 84.3 under the reported 16-shot ViT-B/16 setting. Figure 6(a) values also change. Main benchmark per-dataset scores remain unchanged, while aggregate values are corrected or recomputed for revised difficulty groups.

T1.justification: v1's informal non-crossing-trajectory argument is expanded into Section 4 and Appendix A. These add class-conditional probability-path definitions, Identity and Classification propositions, proofs invoking Lipschitz continuity and ODE uniqueness, and a conditioned training-objective derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a one-step interpretation of existing PEFT methods and a model-agnostic, multi-step FMA framework benefiting difficult datasets. Class correspondence, robustness and early-stopping benefits were already claimed in v1. Abstract wording is streamlined without materially redefining these claims.

C2.justification: The introduction newly interprets improvement over linear probing as separating data access from alignment capability and expands the local-update explanation for flow matching. Section 4 interprets augmentation through nonzero-variance paths and acknowledges that noise can complicate training. Existing early-stopping limitations and sample-specific stopping as future work remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies previously missing velocity-network specifications: a MAR-based architecture with six ResNet blocks, feature-sized hidden dimensions and 200 training epochs. It defines the noise scale, lists selected inference steps by dataset and baseline in Table 6, and adds a code link. The cosine-scheduler disclosure is removed, without establishing an actual scheduler change.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the main research positioning remain substantially unchanged. v3 adds Li et al. (2024) for the MAR architecture and Zhu et al. (2025) for the diffusion-bridge interpretation, while removing the Loshchilov–Hutter AdamW citation.

P1.justification: Editing concentrates on introductory motivation, condensed inference explanations and text-embedding notation. A theoretical-analysis section and appendix organization are introduced, with existing algorithms moved to Appendix B. Most related-work prose, experimental narrative and the conclusion are retained.

P2.justification: The generalization table is substantially expanded, and new Appendix Tables 4–7 display uncertainty, significance, inference settings and transfer breakdowns. Existing benchmark tables reorder Cars and UCF. Several figures and the algorithms are relocated, producing a substantial expansion and reorganization of the paper's visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility through missing architecture, training and inference details, adds statistical context and broader transfer evidence, and corrects erroneous benchmark averages. The net gain is limited by unspecified statistical procedures and remaining inconsistencies, such as CLIP's easy average of 78.8 in Table 3 versus 78.0 in Table 4. The new proofs address idealized paths; their guarantees for the noisy learned solver remain unestablished.
